correctness.rationale: A smooth cubic surface has a rank-seven unimodular geometric Picard lattice generated by lines. The 27 explicit lines and finite-field rank intersections yield a seven-line determinant-one geometric basis. The five Frobenius coefficient patterns follow from cube classes and permutations, and the rational invariant cone is generated by orbit sums. All negative traces have self-intersection strictly less than zero and nonnegative intersection with other traces; the remaining positive traces satisfy the given exact decomposition. The dual-ray enumerator uses all choose(n,r-1) active sets, computes integer null vectors by Bareiss minors, checks all inequalities and deduplicates, producing 99,1,1,21,6. Independent F7 point counts match Picard traces. All claims quantify over nonzero coefficients only; no integral arithmetic basis is asserted.

value.rationale: The full arithmetic nef and Mori face counts control positivity of rational divisor classes in the natural complete diagonal family over F7, including a nontrivial jump from the 15/21-ray rank-five cone to the 6/6-ray rank-three cone. The explicit contraction of three positive trace sums to an interior hyperplane class describes the mechanism, and the classification applies to every nonzero coefficient quadruple rather than an arbitrary isolated example. The result is more than a recomputed point count or textbook rank deduction.
